b2-13-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Will the Count Give Up?
b2-13-01.scenario: A clerk in Beszterce asks you, a town councillor, whether Count Pongrácz will give up his plan against the town.
b2-13-01.prompt: Answer the clerk with careful doubt.
b2-13-01.target: A gróf aligha mond le a tervéről, mert nagyon büszke.
b2-13-01.english: The count will hardly give up his plan, because he is very proud.
b2-13-01.canDo: I can express polite skepticism and mitigating doubt using aligha.

b2-13-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Not Be Afraid
b2-13-02.scenario: A clerk in Beszterce asks you, a town councillor, why people should not be afraid of Count Pongrácz.
b2-13-02.prompt: Calm the clerk by pointing to something everyone knows about the count.
cues: Say there is no need to be afraid
b2-13-02.target: Nem kell félni, hiszen a gróf a szegényeknek pénzt ad.
b2-13-02.english: There is no need to be afraid, after all the count gives money to the poor.
b2-13-02.canDo: I can invoke shared knowledge and background assumptions using hiszen.

b2-13-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Count's Plan
b2-13-03.scenario: A colleague at the town hall of Beszterce asks you what you think of Count Pongrácz's plan to attack the town.
b2-13-03.prompt: Give your opinion of the plan, in a mild way.
cues: Say what you think of the plan
b2-13-03.target: A gróf terve nem éppen okos.
b2-13-03.english: The count's plan is not exactly clever.
b2-13-03.canDo: I can soften criticism with nem éppen.

b2-13-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Count Out of Time
b2-13-04.scenario: A friend from Beszterce asks you how Count Pongrácz behaves.
b2-13-04.prompt: Tell your friend, with irony, how the count behaves.
cues: Compare him to a time that is gone
b2-13-04.target: Úgy viselkedik, mintha még a középkorban élne.
b2-13-04.english: He behaves as if he were still living in the Middle Ages.
b2-13-04.canDo: I can combine conditional verb forms with modal particles (szinte, mintha) to satirize absurd behavior.

b2-13-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Column About the Count
b2-13-05.scenario: Your newspaper in Beszterce asks you for two sentences of a witty column about Count Pongrácz.
b2-13-05.prompt: Write two gently ironic sentences about the count.
cues: Name one thing about the count
b2-13-05.target: A gróf, ugyebár, kemény ember. Mégiscsak a szegényeknek pénzt ad.
b2-13-05.english: The count, as everyone knows, is a hard man. After all, he gives money to the poor.
b2-13-05.canDo: I can write a sophisticated ironic commentary or cultural column (tárca).

b2-13-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Is the Count Dangerous?
b2-13-consolidation.scenario: Apolka asks you, a clerk in Beszterce, whether Count Pongrácz is dangerous.
b2-13-consolidation.prompt: Answer Apolka, and give your reason.
b2-13-consolidation.target: Korántsem veszélyes, hiszen a gróf cseppet sem rossz ember.
b2-13-consolidation.english: He is by no means dangerous, after all the count is not a bad man in the least.
b2-13-consolidation.canDo: I can use aligha, korántsem, and éppenséggel to navigate polite doubt and emphatic denial.
